summary: Greenbrier County enclosed fire tower built 1913-1914 with donated lumber; a 1916 report describes its watchman. Now listed as gone, with no source on the site today.

facts.agency: West Virginia Fish, Game & Forestry Commission
facts.status_note: The register lists the tower as gone; no source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Register gives the build span as 1913-1914; the 1913-14 warden's biennial report credits donated lumber for the Job Knob station.
Report entry (dated 1916 in the transcription) names watchman James H. McMillion, who lived nine miles away and stayed at the station each night.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on January 26, 2017.

notes_for_editor: Record matches the register on location, elevation (4,347 ft) and kind (enclosed tower). Two sources disagree on elevation: the register gives 4,347 ft (1,325 m), while the transcribed 1916 warden report gives 4,388 ft; the story says so and does not pick one. The transcription page headers the report as c.1915 but dates the watchman entry 1916; the story follows the entry date. Build date rests on the register (1913-1914) and the 1913-14 lumber donation, which agree. Removal date, current site condition and access are not found in any source read. Only one search was run beyond the register pages.
